meta: Read that "this company is fine-tuning its own model" and didn't get it? Bit explains in 60 seconds: fine-tuning = extra training, adjusting a model that has already learned, using a special set of examples.
thu: Before you think about fine-tuning, try things in order: prompt → RAG. Write a really clear prompt, then give AI your documents to look things up in. Most tasks are done after these two steps.

muc.title: What is fine-tuning?
muc.text: Mark reads in the news that a company is fine-tuning its own model, and wants to know what fine-tuning means.

muc.title: Extra training for a trained model
muc.text: Bit explains: fine-tuning is extra training, adjusting a model that has already finished learning with a special set of examples. Like someone who finished high school taking a job training course.

muc.title: A real example
muc.text: For example: give it thousands of customer service conversations, and the model learns that company's tone and way of handling things.

muc.title: Different from prompts and RAG
muc.text: It's different from a prompt, which gives instructions every time you ask, or RAG, which lets it look things up in documents, as in video 25. Fine-tuning changes the model's own habits.

muc.title: When you see this word
muc.text: When you see this word, think: extra training for the model. Everyday users rarely need it. Good prompts and good documents solve most things.
